title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is working in the linear (GL(2,Ẑ)) shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller formalism. Triples (α,β,f) in GL(2,Ẑ) are tied together by the 'formule des lacets' ξ = ε y η^ν, where ν is the parameter with μ = 2ν+1 (the analogue of λ = 2m+1 in GT).

The fixed elements, read off the algebra:
- ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], since cρ+d = [[d,c],[-c,c+d]]; ρ has order 6 in SL2.
- σ_∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]], since tσ_∞+u = [[u,t],[-t,u]]; σ_∞ has order 4.
- τ_∞ = diag(1,-1).
- α_2 ∈ Z/2 is defined by (-1)^{α_2} = ε.
- The elements cρ+d and tσ_∞+u are the 'norm-form' units of the centralizers of ρ and σ_∞, i.e. the Eisenstein and Gaussian tori.

The α side. With α = [[a,b],[c,d]] one has α(cρ+d) = [[det α, ac+bc+bd],[0, c²+cd+d²]]. With δ = ε_3 ∈ {±1} and δ·det α = 1, this gives δα(cρ+d) = [[1,B],[0,D]], where:
- B = δ(ac+bc+bd)
- D = δ(c²+cd+d²)

The β side. With β = [[r,s],[t,u]] of determinant 1, β(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^{α_2} = [[1, εS],[0, εU]], where:
- S = rt+su
- U = t²+u²

Consequence. Equation (76), δα(cρ+d) = β(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^{α_2}, is just the pair D = εU, B = εS. Hence the loop relation (69) is equivalent to (76) together with μD = 1. This is the boxed system (72) of the previous page. From it one recovers δ ≡ μ mod 3 and ε ≡ μ mod 4, i.e. δ = ε_3(μ) and ε = ε_2(μ). It also follows that α_2 is read off from δ(c²+cd+d²) mod 4, since D is a unit with ε ≡ D^{-1} ≡ D mod 4.

Definition (78). u_{α,β} := μδ·α(cρ+d) = μβ(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^{α_2} = [[μ, μB],[0,1]]. This is an element of the Borel subgroup with diagonal (μ,1), i.e. of 'cyclotomic' type. It depends only on α (μ = D^{-1}, B from α), or equivalently only on β plus the sign α_2.

Purpose. Because cρ+d centralizes ρ and tσ_∞+u centralizes σ_∞ (with τ_∞ inverting σ_∞), the single matrix u_{α,β} conjugates ρ to int(α)(ρ) and σ_∞ to int(β)(σ_∞^{±1}). In other words, the pair of 'local' conjugations (α at the order-6 point, β at the order-4 point) is realized by one global element of the form diag(μ,1)·unipotent. The next page twists this by f (u_{α,β,f} = f^{-1}u_{α,β}) and derives u(ε_0) = ε·ε_0^μ for ε_0 = σ_∞ρ. This is the GL2/SL2(Ẑ) analogue of the statement that a GT-element acts on the triangle-group generators by conjugates of λ-th powers.

Margin. Grothendieck observes that u_{α,β} depends on β only through a sign, linked to the image in SL(2,Ẑ)^{ab}, and refers forward to p. 410.
errors: In the matrix line explicating δα(cρ+d), the right-hand side is written as δ·[[1,B],[0,D]] (or with a symbol resembling δ/ξ). For consistency with (78) and with (73) of the previous page (c²+cd+d² = δ/μ), one must have δα(cρ+d) = [[1,B],[0,D]], with det α = δ and D = δ(c²+cd+d²). The extra factor on the right is a slip.

Sign subtlety: τ_∞ σ_∞ τ_∞^{-1} = σ_∞^{-1} = -σ_∞. So conjugation by u_{α,β} gives u(σ_∞) = int(β)(σ_∞^{(-1)^{α_2}}) = ε·int(β)(σ_∞), not int(β)(σ_∞) as asserted in (81) on the next page. The factor ε reappears in (83), so the overall bookkeeping is recoverable, but (80)/(81) as written are off by the sign ε when α_2 is odd.
Minor: '(α=α_2)' in the exponent of τ_∞ conflates the matrix α with the exponent α_2 ∈ Z/2. This is notational only.

ideas.what: Reduction of the loop relation, in its GL(2,Ẑ) image, to the scalar equations D = εU, B = εS, μD = 1, via the centralizer tori of ρ (Eisenstein units c²+cd+d²) and σ_∞ (Gaussian units t²+u²).
ideas.modern_name: Linear/abelianized (SL2(Ẑ)) shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller hexagon/loop relations; norm forms of CM tori in GL2
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT group: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; actions on SL2-type quotients: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse; La Longue Marche (1981) discusses the formalism in general terms, but this computation is unsure there

ideas.what: Construction of a single Borel element u_{α,β} = [[μ, μB],[0,1]] realizing simultaneously the conjugations of the order-6 generator ρ by α and of the order-4 generator σ_∞ by β (up to sign), with u(σ_∞ρ) = ε(σ_∞ρ)^μ.
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic-type (Borel) automorphism of SL2(Ẑ) induced by a GT-like element; 'inner up to diag(λ,1)'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the GT literature on the action on SL2(Ẑ) and congruence completions (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura); unsure of an exact first source

ideas.what: Determination of the signs δ = ε_3(μ) and ε = ε_2(μ) by μ mod 3 and mod 4, and of α_2 by δ(c²+cd+d²) mod 4.
ideas.modern_name: Characters of Ẑ^× of conductor 3 and 4 attached to the elliptic points of order 3 and 2

missed.claim: This is a fully explicit matrix-level treatment by Grothendieck of the GL(2,Ẑ)/SL(2,Ẑ) image of the loop (lacets) relation. It shows the relation is equivalent to D = εU, B = εS, μD = 1, with the realizing element u_{α,β} in the Borel subgroup diag(μ,1)·unipotent. The content is elementary and consistent with later GT results. It is of documentary rather than mathematical novelty: it shows Grothendieck testing the 'équation des lacets' on the congruence (linear) quotient before the GT literature.
missed.quote: u_{α,β} = (μδ).α(cρ+d) = μβ(tσ_∞+u)τ_∞^α = μ(1 B; 0 D) = (μ μB; 0 1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for the GT action on SL2(Ẑ) and modular towers. It shows that Grothendieck tracked the explicit sign characters ε_2, ε_3 attached to the elliptic points.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful and correct (up to a sign slip) linear-algebra computation in GL(2,Ẑ) that is the routine abelian shadow of the GT loop relation. It is consistent with later known results and contains no new theorem, but it documents Grothendieck's explicit treatment.
transcription_corrections: Under (δ) in (76) the subscript reads 'δ = ε_3 ∈ {±1}' (δ written over ε_3 with an equality sign).
Second line: 'où α_2 = α_ε est défini par la condition (-1)^{α_2} = ε (= ε_2)'.
The β-matrix: the first entry is overwritten (r?). For the algebra to work, β = [[r,s],[t,u]] with det β = 1 (giving S = rt+su, U = t²+u²); the signs '-S', '-t' as read are doubtful.
Right-hand side of the α-computation: the leading symbol before (1 B; 0 D) is ambiguous (δ or ξ). Mathematically it should be absent.
'(69, 69)' is probably '(69), (69 bis)' or similar reference to the loop relation equations.
'mod 4' at the end of 'la valeur de δ(c²+cd+d²) mod 4' is confirmed by the mathematics (ε ≡ μ ≡ D mod 4).
Margin begins: 'en fait, u_{α,β} ne dépend que de α, et de β que via ...' and ends 'je ne vais pas ... cf. p. 410'. It also mentions the image in Sl(2,Ẑ)^{ab} and a sign condition.
